answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so influence depends on reachable honest attestations, not merely on the number of identities. A sybil cluster may look velvet-smooth internally, yet its sparse external cut gives it low conductance: few walks cross its boundary. Min-cut transitivity bounds then cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight by that limited boundary flow, even if it builds a jetty of fake nodes; the nadir of trust remains constrained by independent connections.
